events: Gary rolled his golf cart onto the street and is testing a new speaker; a few seconds of Jimmy Buffett blared before he turned it down.
Donna added two new flamingos to her front yard, bringing the visible flock to seven.
Hal is standing at the mailbox kiosk, looking from Gary's cart to Donna's flamingos.
Rosa crossed the street holding a stack of handwritten dinner invitations.

reflections: Since Linda passed, the garage is where I feel most like myself.
Hal doesn't like me much, but nobody on this street knows wiring like I do.
memories: [Tick -40] Bought a 200-watt marine speaker and two strings of LED rope light for the cart.
[Tick -12] Donna asked if I'd ever played pickleball. I said no and changed the subject.
[Tick -3] Read the parade flyer at the Town Square: sign-ups close at the end of the month.

reflections: Partners make or break your ladder ranking, and mine keep moving to Ocala.
Gary has quick hands and nothing to do on weekends. He just doesn't know he wants to play yet.
memories: [Tick -20] Dropped from 4th to 6th on the ladder after my partner moved away.
[Tick -12] Asked Gary about pickleball; he dodged the question.
[Tick -5] Heard at book club that Hal filed a complaint about someone's mailbox last spring.

reflections: Rules exist so neighbors don't have to argue. Somebody has to keep them.
The street was quieter before the new speaker arrived.
memories: [Tick -30] Wrote 'Kowalski cart: lights + wiring, no approval?' in the notebook.
[Tick -8] Counted five flamingos in Pruitt's yard. Limit is three.
[Tick -2] Rosa waved at me from her driveway. Waved back. Didn't know what else to do.

reflections: I moved here to slow down, and so far I've worked four shifts and met nobody.
These three neighbors clearly have history I don't understand yet.
memories: [Tick -15] Gary fixed my garbage disposal and refused to take any money.
[Tick -10] Donna invited me to three clubs in one conversation.
[Tick -1] Hal told me my recycling bin was facing the wrong way. He was right.
